prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Houston, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1216; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine. We'll keep it brief. Where were you when the collision happened?
A: I was on the main road in Houston, heading toward the highway entrance. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me.
Q: What was the weather and visibility like?
A: It was clear. The roads were dry, and it was still daylight.
Q: Tell me what happened in your own words.
A: I stopped behind a car at a light. I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped back against the headrest. The car in front of me was pushed a little, but I stayed where I was.
Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?
A: No. I was looking at the light and my mirror didn't show anything close enough to worry about.
Q: Did you get out of the vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, I got out and talked to the other driver. He said he was looking at his phone for a second.
Q: Were there any police or emergency responders present?
A: An officer came after about twenty minutes and wrote something down. I'm not sure what it said.
Q: How are you feeling now?
A: My lower back is sore and stiff, especially when I sit for long periods. My neck is a bit tight too. I've started seeing a doctor for it.
Q: Have you had any prior injuries to your back?
A: I had a minor strain years ago, but it healed and I hadn't had trouble with it recently.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Only that I want my car repaired and my medical bills taken care of. I'm willing to send you my records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
